background_task.longDescription: Running Claude Code in background or headless mode enables automated task execution without requiring an interactive terminal session. This powerful capability allows you to queue up complex operations, run batch processing jobs, or integrate Claude into CI/CD pipelines. Background mode transforms Claude from an interactive assistant into an autonomous agent that can handle tasks while you focus on other work.
background_task.whyItMatters: Background execution unlocks automation scenarios like nightly code reviews, batch file processing, and integration with build systems. It transforms Claude from a conversation partner into a powerful automation engine.

howTo.summary: Use the --background flag or headless mode to run Claude without an interactive terminal.

steps.instruction: Run Claude with a specific task in background mode

code.content: claude --background --print "Analyze all TypeScript files for type errors"

steps.instruction: Use headless mode for scripted automation

code.content: claude --headless -p "Review the latest commit and write a summary" > review.md

steps.instruction: Combine with output redirection for batch jobs

code.content: claude --print --output-format json "List all TODO comments" > todos.json

examples.title: Automated Code Review Script
examples.description: Run code review on new commits in CI

code.content:
#!/bin/bash
# ci-review.sh - Run Claude code review in CI pipeline
git diff HEAD~1 > /tmp/changes.diff
claude --headless --print "Review these changes for bugs and security issues: $(cat /tmp/changes.diff)" > review-report.md

examples.explanation: This script captures the diff from the last commit and sends it to Claude for review in headless mode.

tips: Use --print flag to output results to stdout for piping
Combine with --output-format json for machine-readable output
Set reasonable timeouts for background tasks to avoid runaway processes

bypass_mode.longDescription: The bypassPermissions setting allows you to skip interactive permission prompts for specific tools or all tools during a session. This is particularly useful for automation scenarios, trusted environments, or when you have established confidence in Claude's tool usage patterns. While powerful, this feature should be used thoughtfully to maintain appropriate oversight of Claude's actions.
bypass_mode.whyItMatters: Permission prompts ensure safety but can interrupt workflow in trusted scenarios. Bypass mode enables smoother automation while still letting you configure exactly which permissions to grant automatically.

howTo.summary: Configure bypassPermissions in settings.json to automatically approve specific tool operations.

steps.instruction: Create or edit your Claude settings file
Add bypassPermissions for specific tools
Or bypass all permissions for fully automated mode

examples.title: Safe Read-Only Bypass
examples.description: Allow all read operations while prompting for writes
examples.explanation: This configuration auto-approves read operations while still requiring confirmation for file modifications and command execution.

tips: Start with read-only tool bypasses before adding write permissions
Use project-level settings for project-specific bypass rules
Consider using allowedTools instead for more granular control
gotchas: Full bypass mode should only be used in isolated/sandboxed environments
Always review what tools are being bypassed before enabling

compact_mode.longDescription: The /compact command summarizes your conversation history into a condensed form, freeing up context window space while preserving the essential information Claude needs to continue helping you effectively. This is particularly valuable during long sessions where you have accumulated substantial context from file reads, code exploration, and discussions.
compact_mode.whyItMatters: Claude has a finite context window. As conversations grow, older context gets truncated. Using /compact lets you strategically preserve important information while making room for new work.

howTo.summary: Use /compact when your context window is filling up to summarize and free space.

steps.instruction: Check your current context usage with /context
When context is high (>70%), run /compact to summarize
Optionally provide instructions for what to preserve

code.content: /compact Focus on preserving the API schema details and implementation decisions

examples.title: Compact with Custom Focus
examples.description: Preserve specific context during compaction

code.content: /compact Keep the database schema, the API endpoints we discussed, and the test failures we identified

examples.explanation: Adding specific instructions helps Claude prioritize what to retain in the summary.

tips: Run /context before /compact to see how much space you will reclaim
Use descriptive instructions to guide what context to preserve
Consider compacting before starting a major new task in the same session

context_watcher.longDescription: The /context command displays your current context window usage, showing how much of Claude's available memory is being used by the conversation history, file contents, and system context. Understanding your context usage helps you make informed decisions about when to compact, start fresh, or be more selective about what files to read.
context_watcher.whyItMatters: Context awareness prevents unexpected truncation of important information. Knowing when you are approaching limits lets you proactively manage the conversation for optimal results.

howTo.summary: Use /context to view your current context window utilization.

steps.instruction: Run the context command to see current usage
Review the output showing tokens used and available

examples.explanation: Checking context before adding large amounts of content helps avoid losing important earlier context.

tips: Check context periodically during long sessions
High context usage (>70%) suggests it is time to /compact
Consider starting a new session if context is critically full

cost_tracker.longDescription: The /cost command displays your API usage and associated costs for the current session and cumulative usage. This transparency helps you understand the economic impact of your Claude interactions, make informed decisions about usage patterns, and optimize your workflows to balance productivity with cost efficiency.
cost_tracker.whyItMatters: Understanding costs enables smarter usage decisions. Track which types of tasks consume more tokens so you can optimize expensive operations and budget effectively.

howTo.summary: Use /cost to view your current and cumulative API usage costs.

steps.instruction: Run the cost command to see session spending
Review both session and total usage

This is ideal for individual preferences, local environment settings, or temporary configurations that should not affect your team. The local settings merge with project settings, giving you personalized control without polluting shared configuration.
local_override.whyItMatters: Local overrides let you personalize Claude without affecting teammates. Keep your vim mode, custom permissions, or experimental settings separate from shared project configuration.

Monorepos contain multiple packages, applications, or services within a single repository, requiring Claude to navigate between distinct modules while maintaining awareness of shared dependencies and cross-package relationships.
mono_repo_master.whyItMatters: Monorepos are common in enterprise environments. Claude's ability to navigate multi-package architectures enables effective assistance across complex codebases with interdependent modules.

Each project provides unique context, and Claude adapts to different codebases, languages, frameworks, and conventions. This breadth of usage builds experience with Claude's capabilities across diverse scenarios.

You can configure Claude for verbose explanatory output, minimal concise responses, or other styles that match your preferences and workflow needs. This customization helps Claude's communication style match your expectations.

permission_config.longDescription: Configuring default permissions in Claude Code allows you to pre-authorize certain operations while maintaining safety boundaries. The permissions system controls which tools Claude can use automatically versus which require explicit approval. Thoughtful permission configuration balances workflow efficiency with appropriate oversight.
permission_config.whyItMatters: Permission configuration puts you in control of Claude's autonomy level. Well-configured permissions reduce interruptions while maintaining safety for sensitive operations.

permission_sculptor.longDescription: Granular tool-specific permissions represent advanced Claude Code configuration. Rather than broad allow/deny rules, permission sculpting lets you specify exact patterns for MCP tools, bash commands, and file operations. This precision enables sophisticated automation workflows while maintaining tight security boundaries around sensitive operations.
permission_sculptor.whyItMatters: Granular permissions enable sophisticated automation without compromising security. You can auto-approve specific MCP tools while requiring confirmation for others from the same server.

plan_creator.longDescription: Creating plan files establishes structured documentation for complex tasks, features, or projects. Plan files in Claude Code provide a shared understanding between you and Claude about goals, approach, and progress. They serve as persistent memory across sessions and help organize multi-step work into manageable phases.
plan_creator.whyItMatters: Plans transform vague ideas into actionable roadmaps. A good plan file gives Claude context to make better decisions and helps you track progress across sessions.

howTo.summary: Create markdown plan files in .claude/plans/ or a project plans/ directory.

steps.instruction: Create the plans directory
Create a plan file for your feature or task

code.content:
# Authentication System Plan

## Goals
- Implement JWT-based authentication
- Add OAuth2 social login
- Create password reset flow

## Phases
1. [ ] Setup JWT infrastructure
2. [ ] Implement login/register endpoints
3. [ ] Add social OAuth providers
4. [ ] Build password reset

## Technical Decisions
- Using jose library for JWT
- Storing refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies

steps.instruction: Reference the plan in your Claude sessions

code.content: Let's continue working on the auth system plan - we're on phase 2

examples.title: Feature Implementation Plan

## Overview
Add full-text search to the blog platform.

## Requirements
- Search posts by title and content
- Filter by date, author, tags
- Highlight matched terms

## Implementation
1. [ ] Add search index (Elasticsearch/Meilisearch)
2. [ ] Create search API endpoint
3. [ ] Build search UI component
4. [ ] Add result highlighting

## Progress
- 2024-01-15: Started phase 1, chose Meilisearch

examples.explanation: This plan provides clear goals, phases, and a progress log for tracking work across sessions.

tips: Use checkboxes [ ] to track completed phases
Include technical decisions and their rationale
Update plans as requirements evolve

plan_mode.longDescription: Plan mode is a special Claude Code mode focused on planning and thinking through problems before implementation. Activated with /plan or Shift+Tab, it encourages Claude to reason through approaches, consider alternatives, and outline strategies without immediately jumping to code. This deliberate planning phase often leads to better solutions.
plan_mode.whyItMatters: Planning before coding prevents wasted effort on wrong approaches. Plan mode encourages thoughtful analysis of problems, resulting in better architecture and fewer rewrites.

howTo.summary: Enter plan mode with /plan or Shift+Tab to focus Claude on thinking and planning.

steps.instruction: Enter plan mode at the start of a complex task

plan_strategist.whyItMatters: Multiple plans enable parallel workstreams and clear boundaries between features. Each plan can evolve independently, making it easier to context-switch and track progress.
